title: LogLevelRequest
description:
Change the running process's log level without restarting it (PUT /v1/admin/log-level body). At least one of `level` or `loggers` must be present; a body carrying neither is a 422, because a request that asks for nothing is far more likely a typo than an intent. Validation is atomic: the whole body is checked before anything is applied, so a rejected request leaves the effective level exactly as it was — there is no half-applied state.

`ttl_seconds` adds an expiry to the change. Every PUT SUPERSEDES the previous one, expiry included: any pending auto-revert is cancelled first, and a new one is armed only if this body carries `ttl_seconds`. Two overlapping TTLs therefore cannot exist and cannot fight. The corollary is worth reading twice — a follow-up PUT that omits `ttl_seconds` DISARMS the expiry the earlier one armed. That is visible immediately in the response (`auto_revert_pending: false`) and on the WARNING audit line, which carries the `ttl_seconds`/`expires_at` columns for every change including the ones that clear them.

level.description: New ROOT log level. Case-insensitive; `warn` is accepted as an alias for `WARNING` because .env.example has documented it since before LOG_LEVEL was honoured at all. `NOTSET` is rejected here: on the root logger it means 'no threshold' rather than 'inherit', and turning every library in the process to full DEBUG is not what an operator typing it would expect. Deliberately NOT an `enum`: the server validates the vocabulary and answers a 4xx, and an enum here would make that documented response unreachable from a conformant client. That is `UserRoleRequest.role`'s reasoning — note it answers 400 there and this answers 422, because `admin_users.py` reserves 400 for a malformed request to keep it distinct from the 409 its state change can raise, and this endpoint has no such neighbour. The response DOES pin the enum, because there the server is the writer. Omit to leave the root level as it is.

loggers.description: Per-logger overrides, as a name -> level map. REPLACE semantics: whatever is sent becomes the complete set of runtime per-logger overrides, so `{}` clears them all and there is no separate 'unset one logger' verb. Any logger previously overridden and absent here is returned to inheriting (NOTSET) before the root level and the dampen set are re-applied on top. Omit the whole field to leave the current overrides untouched. Names are validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$` and must ALREADY EXIST in the process's logger registry — `logging.getLogger(name)` creates a logger permanently, so accepting arbitrary names would make this endpoint an unbounded-growth path even behind the admin gate. The count is capped (see `max_logger_overrides` in the response). `ragstack.audit` cannot be overridden: it carries this endpoint's own audit trail.

ttl_seconds.description: Auto-revert this change after N seconds. Absent or null means NO expiry — exactly the behaviour this endpoint has always had, unchanged. When set, the process reverts to the CONFIGURED defaults at the deadline: the same end state DELETE produces, not a restoration of whatever was in force before this PUT. So an override an operator had deliberately set beforehand is dropped at expiry too; re-send it if you want it back. The revert is audited at WARNING as `audit=expired` (distinct from an operator's `audit=reset`), carrying the principal that armed it — a level change nobody typed has to be explainable afterwards. Bounds are 1..86400 (24h): a TTL is for a debugging session an operator is present for, and a day bounds the blast radius of a forgotten DEBUG, which is the failure this field exists to prevent (measured: httpcore emits ~15 lines per outbound HTTP call at DEBUG and DEBUG releases the dampen set, so one /v1/query goes from ~3 lines to 75-210). Anything longer is a `LOG_LEVEL` change plus a restart, which is reviewable and survives the process. The server validates the range and answers 422 with `{"detail": "<sentence>"}`, atomically with the rest of the body; the bounds are declared here as documentation, the way `loggers.maxProperties` mirrors `max_logger_overrides`. A body carrying ONLY `ttl_seconds` is refused: a TTL modifies a change, it is not one. The pending expiry is PROCESS-LOCAL like the rest of this state — a restart reverts everything anyway, which is the same feature stated a different way.
